description: The adventure layer (WP16): what rooms, characters and items say, the cutter-die chain in the Cookie Machine's chain data (data/chains/cookie_machine.json names these ids), Red Panda's hint per chain step, and a caption for each Cookie Machine part as it starts working. expression picks the portrait. where room:<id> is the room it belongs to; when interaction means a tap or drop names it by id; hint means Red Panda's help.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Tea? Sit, rest, then go and find each other.
Everyone here is missing a piece. That's how you find each other.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Stuck? Come and talk to me. I always have a hint and a cushion.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: The lucky word board. Tell me the word on your fortune.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: The kettle sings when it is happy. It is nearly always happy.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: The cutter is cutting! Ask your crew what else is still broken.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: A paper lantern sways. Warm light, no wires.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: THE TEAHOUSE
Tea, cushions and lucky words.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: PENGUIN'S WORKSHOP
Knock. Flap. Enter.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: PARCEL DEPOT
Everything gets there. Eventually.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: SCRAPYARD
Look-alike parts. No returns. (Returns welcome.)

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: A wishing well. Somebody has wished for documentation.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: A little boat called Pull Request. It is waiting for review.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The Fortune Machine, waiting for its crew.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The Oven, cold and quiet, waiting for its crew.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: Nothing happens. That does not go there.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Flap flap. Workshop. Tools. Bench. Mind the oil.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: The press should go thump. If it goes thunk, something's wrong.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: My bench. Good for straightening bent things. Tap tap.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Spanners, mallets, one lonely sock. Don't ask about the sock.

pieces.speaker: Gopher
lines: Well, hello there! Parcels in, parcels out.

pieces.speaker: Gopher
lines: Every cookie gets a wrapper and a ride. That's my promise.

pieces.speaker: Gopher
lines: Rows of lockers. The gnu's is the yellow one, number 3.

pieces.speaker: Gopher
lines: Misdelivered parcels. One is addressed to The Cloud. Ask me how I know.

pieces.speaker: Seagull
lines: Squawk! Fortunes, scraps, lost bits. I keep them all!

pieces.speaker: Seagull
lines: My nest! Paper scraps, string, half a fortune. Don't touch. Okay, touch.

pieces.speaker: Crab
lines: Hi! I merge every fix. Sideways, but I merge it.

pieces.speaker: Crab
lines: Each fix is a patch. Patches make the machines everyone's, not one gnu's.

pieces.speaker: Crab
lines: The contributors board! Every fixer's name goes up here.

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: Welcome to the harbour, home of FortuneCloud!

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: My briefcase holds the future. It is stuck, but it holds it.

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: FREE TRIAL, says the lure. The small print says a lot more.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: My spanner. For tightening things that wobble.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: The cutter die, bent in the post. My bench can fix that.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: The cutter die, straight again. Twelve good teeth.

pieces.speaker: Seagull
lines: A scrap in the gnu's writing: LOCKER 2 4 1.
Seagull found it in the spring. It is dated March 3.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: A look-alike die from the scrapyard. It has 10 teeth.

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: The FortuneCloud die! Its connector is a shape you have never seen.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Die out for sharpening. - G.
(Back Tuesday. Which Tuesday? Good question.)

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The die drops into the cutter. Now tighten its bolts.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The die wobbles in the cutter. It needs tightening, and you have no spanner.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: Nothing to tighten. The cutter has no die.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The bent die will not sit flat. It would jam. Straighten it first.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: This die has 10 teeth. The plate on the cutter says 12.
Close, but no cookie.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The FortuneCloud die's shiny connector fits nothing in the cutter.
(On the back: SUBSCRIPTION REQUIRED.)

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Thump. Thump. Thump. Hear that? The cutter is cutting!

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Rounds, rounds, rounds. Good cutter.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Sharpening? Flap. The gnu never sharpened anything here.
Try the depot. He mailed everything. Gopher keeps the lockers.
Take my spanner. You'll need it to tighten the die.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Lost the spanner? Here. I have another. I always have another.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: The depot. Gopher. Lockers. Go go.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Bent? Put it on my bench. Then tap the bent teeth flat. Tap tap.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Straight as a herring. Into the cutter with it, then tighten.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Count the teeth. Ten. The cutter wants twelve. Scrapyard special.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Shiny. Fits nothing. Anglerfish special. Give it back to him.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: On the bench. Now the mallet: tap each bent tooth.

pieces.speaker: Penguin
lines: Flap flap! Straight as a fish. Now it can cut.

pieces.speaker: Gnu
lines: Locker code: my batter, read off the jars.
Egg's jar, then vanilla's, then sugar's. One digit each.
(Changed it this summer. New code, new me.) - G.

pieces.speaker: Gopher
lines: The gnu's locker? Number 3, yellow, with a code lock.
He changed the code a while back. Ask me how I know.

pieces.speaker: Gopher
lines: Empty now. Just a smell of vanilla. Ask me how I know.

pieces.speaker: Gopher
lines: That scrap? Old as my hat. The gnu changed his code since.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: Click! The locker opens. A parcel for the gnu.
Inside: the cutter die. It is bent.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The locker screen flashes: CODE CHANGED.
PARCEL FORWARDED: HARBOUR.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The locker beeps. Not that code.

pieces.speaker: Seagull
lines: Squawk! The gnu's locker code? Got it right here!
Found it in the spring. Take it, take it.

pieces.speaker: Seagull
lines: Old? Squawk. It WAS a spring scrap.
Some things I know word for word. Dates, not so much.

pieces.speaker: Seagull
lines: Back in the nest it goes. Squawk.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: A cutter die in the junk! It looks right... mostly.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: Springs, cogs, a teapot lid. Nothing else that fits.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: Back on the pile it goes. No harm done.

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: Forwarded here? Wonderful! FortuneCloud forwards every old code.
Fancy a FortuneCloud die? Compatible with all your old codes!

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: FortuneCloud slip: old locker codes come here. Dated September 12.
Seagull's scrap is from March, before the gnu changed his code.
The new code is in the batter. Your crew's fortunes know it.

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: A FortuneCloud cutter die! Gleaming, modern, yours on a free trial.

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: No refunds! Kidding. Here, I'll take it back.

pieces.speaker: Anglerfish
lines: Old codes? We love old codes. We forward them all here.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: The Cookie Machine's cutter is missing something. Have a look in the shop.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Tap the cutter on the Cookie Machine. The gnu left a sticky label on it.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Who knows the Cookie Machine's moving parts? Penguin, in the workshop.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Tell Penguin about the sticky label. The workshop faces the shop on the square.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: The die went to the depot. The gnu's locker has a code lock.
Gopher says the gnu changed the code a while back.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: The code is in the batter: fix the jar shelf with your crew's fortunes.
If the locker sent you to the harbour, compare the dates.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: A bent die? Penguin has a bench for that.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Drag the bent die onto Penguin's bench, then tap the bent teeth flat.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Take the straight die back to the Cookie Machine in the shop.

pieces.speaker: Red Panda
lines: Drag the die onto the cutter, then turn its bolts with Penguin's spanner.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The batter hopper fills. Five jars stand in a row.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The mixer paddle starts to turn.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The control panel blinks through its steps.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The gnu's note glows. The mixer hums along.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The cutter stamps out rounds onto the belt.

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: Penguin's lamp lights up. Flap flap!

pieces.speaker: Narrator
lines: The whole Cookie Machine runs! Rounds roll along toward the Oven.
